headline: Revenue tops guidance, refinancing dents earnings
summary_short: MKS Instruments' Q1 FY2026 revenue rose to $1,078M (+4.4% q/q, +15.2% y/y), landing at the high end of its own guidance, but GAAP net income fell 21.5% q/q to $84M ($1.18 diluted EPS) as one-time debt-refinancing charges and a tax-provision swing weighed on the bottom line.
summary_long: Revenue of $1,078M (+4.4% q/q, +15.2% y/y) landed at the high end of MKS's guidance, with growth broad-based across Semiconductor ($466M), Electronics & Packaging ($321M) and Specialty Industrial ($291M). Gross margin held near 47%. GAAP net income fell to $84M (-21.5% q/q) as $18M of debt-refinancing fees and a $5M loss on extinguishment of debt weighed, alongside a swing to an $18M tax provision from a prior-quarter tax benefit. During the quarter MKS refinanced roughly $1.3B of term-loan debt, issued €1.0B of 2034 senior notes, upsized its revolver to $1.0B, and raised its quarterly dividend to $0.25/share. For Q2 FY2026, MKS guided revenue to $1,200M ± $40M and Adjusted EBITDA to $328M ± $26M, both above Q1 levels.

drivers.explanation: Management attributes the quarter's strength and Q2 outlook to accelerating, broad-based demand tied to AI-related investment across semiconductor and advanced circuit-board manufacturing.
Growth was broad-based across all three segments: Semiconductor $466M (from $435M/$413M), Electronics & Packaging $321M (from $303M/$253M), Specialty Industrial $291M (from $295M/$270M).
GAAP net income fell q/q on $18M of debt-refinancing fees, a $5M loss on extinguishment of debt, and a swing to an $18M tax provision from a prior-quarter tax benefit.
MKS prepaid ~$1.3B of term-loan B and refinanced its EUR term loan using proceeds from a new €1.0B senior notes offering, reducing long-term debt.
The $1.4B convertible senior notes became convertible at holders' option after the stock-price trigger was met in Q1, so they were reclassified from long-term to short-term debt.
